summary: Unexpected discount fractionation from cross-queue pricing merge
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightAssist reports that several hourly invoice lines show a discounted amount that does not match the Console estimate. Discount appears split across multiple invoice lines and a provisional credit was applied automatically, but totals do not reconcile to expected committed discount for dedicated plan.

Impact:
- Immediate customer confusion and billing escalation from finance team.
- Invoice for period 2026-03-01 to 2026-03-07 contains three lines with fractional discount allocations totaling $982.74 but Console estimate shows $1,150.00.
- Customer requests explanation and provisional adjustment to reach expected discount.

Environment:
- Dedicated account in prod (us-east).
- Usage pattern: microburst-heavy embed batches + synchronous chat traffic routed between two queues (high-priority and best-effort).

Observed behavior:
- Rate-selector applied the dedicated discount to the high-priority queue correctly but a tag normalization change from the 2026-03-02 deploy caused a subset of microbatches to be classified under a merged temporary pricing tag. Those lines received a partial, different discount tier leading to fractionation of the expected discount.

Expected behavior:
- All usage for the customer during the billing window should have been apportioned to the contracted dedicated discount and appear as a single discount line on invoice breakouts (or reconcile to same total).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Re-run postback ingestion for org BrightAssist (org_id: org_48b7) for window 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z to 2026-03-07T23:59:59Z with strict ordering flag.
2) Apply current rate-selector logic against raw postbacks and compare to archived pre-deploy selector outputs (sha-1: 9f4c2a).
3) Inspect tag normalization logs for timeframe 2026-03-02 01:00-03:00 UTC (deploy window).

Invoice lines of interest:
- INV-2026-03-07-2345: chat-hosted-rate line, discount -$662.00
- INV-2026-03-07-2346: batch-embed microbatch line, discount -$210.74
- INV-2026-03-07-2360: kv-warmup line, discount -$110.00

Logs and evidence:
- Attached console snapshot (console-snap-214999-0309.png).
- Postback IDs: pb-9981212, pb-9981213, pb-9981214 referenced in audit.
- Slack thread: #support (https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C03SUPPORT/p1678152000000).
steps_to_reproduce: Re-run postback ingestion for org org_48b7 for 2026-03-01 to 2026-03-07 with strict ordering
Apply rate-selector binary v1.22 (pre-deploy sha-1: 9f4c2a) and compare outputs
Query tag-normalizer logs for 2026-03-02 01:00-03:00 UTC and filter for org_48b7 postbacks

comments: 2026-03-10 - Support - Lena Ortiz: Opened with customer, requested billing window and invoice exports. Customer provided CSV and console screenshots.
2026-03-11 - Billing - Priya Malhotra: Verified discrepancy, provisional credit auto-applied by billing guard (credit id CR-2026-03-11-77). We are reproducing selectors locally.
2026-03-11 - Engineering - Marcus Chen: Found tag-normalizer churn during deploy on 2026-03-02; creating reproducible replay. Linking to INT task for filter rollback: INT-330.

2026-03-12 - Support - Lena Ortiz: Informed customer that investigation shows a deploy-induced tag normalization issue, provisional credit of $982.74 remains until final reconciliation. Customer asks for ETA on permanent fix.
investigation_notes: 03/11 09:10 - Replayed postbacks with pre-deploy selector; totals match expected $1,150.00 discount when pre-deploy tags used.
03/11 11:30 - Replayed with current selector and saw three separate discount lines that sum to $982.74. Difference of $167.26 corresponds to microbatches tagged 'dedicated:tmp-merge-03-02'.

03/11 14:00 - Root cause hypothesis: tag-normalizer merged a short-lived temporary tag namespace into pricing namespace during deploy which caused rate-selector to consider those postbacks as different pricing cohort (falls into a lower discount tier).
03/12 08:45 - Confirmed via postback payloads that pb-9981213 contains 'pricing_tag':'dedicated:tmp-merge-03-02'.
03/12 10:00 - Cross-checked with accounting: provisional credit applied by automation; manual adjustment required to finalize invoice if root cause confirmed.
resolution: Provisional credit CR-2026-03-11-77 of $982.74 remains applied to customer invoice pending final reconciliation. Engineering has rolled back the tag-normalizer change in INT (rollback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/812) and scheduled a full re-ingestion for affected window. Accounting will post a corrective invoice adjustment for the missing $167.26 once re-ingestion confirms totals. Follow-ups: create a runbook to block transient tag merges during billing windows (CON-PREROLL-214999) and add a post-deploy smoke that validates invoice totals vs Console estimates. Customer notified on 2026-03-12 and will receive final confirmation within 48 hours.
